retrieved_memory.body: Rivet has learned to recognize Patch's excitement about a project as an early warning that Patch is about to start experimenting before the details are settled.
retrieved_memory.source_episode_title: Patch tries to teach Rivet something ridiculous.

candidates.body_prefix: the agent Patch wired to the workshop thinks it runs the place.
The workshop agent began deciding which of Patch's projects…
The workshop agent began rearranging the order of Patch's projects…
Because it had an opinion about our work. An uninvited opinion…
Rivet has learned to recognize Patch's excitement about a project…
Patch accepted Rivet taking the lead on an experiment…
While Patch was out, Rivet found that the workshop agent had quietly built a folder named 'PATCH OVERRIDES'…
Patch decided the workshop should create a mascot as a character-consistency experiment.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: You built something overnight, placed it beside the 3D printer, and covered it with a towel. That is not how harmless projects begin.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: It is harmless. Probably. I made a little workshop helper that's supposed to notice when something interesting happens and leave us a message.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: "Interesting" is doing a great deal of work in that sentence. What message has it left?

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Three so far. "Printer thinking." "Patch has returned with snacks." And, at 2:14 this morning, "The room is suspiciously quiet."

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: So it observes the workshop, then forms opinions about it. You built a tiny judgmental narrator.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: I built an experiment. Maybe it can catch the weird moment before we miss it—the printer acting odd, an automation doing something unexpected, whatever.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Maybe. But those messages do not tell us whether it noticed anything useful. They tell us it enjoys prose.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Fair. We give it one job. Watch the printer. If anything changes, it has to say exactly what changed. No poetry. No snack surveillance.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Good. Change one thing: start a print. Then we see whether it reports an event, or merely develops a literary career.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Starting it now. Look at that—its little light is blinking. Well… now I want to try it.

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Patch
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: It says: "Printer started. Patch is watching me watch it."

accepted_dialogue_lines.speaker: Rivet
accepted_dialogue_lines.text: Well. It has identified the first problem.

memory_influence_analysis.memory_body: Rivet has learned to recognize Patch's excitement about a project as an early warning that Patch is about to start experimenting before the details are settled.
memory_influence_analysis.no_explicit_callback: The dialogue never quotes the memory, never references a past 'Patch tries to teach Rivet something ridiculous' scene, and never says 'Rivet remembered that…'.

behavioral_manifestations.speaker: Rivet
behavioral_manifestations.manifestation: Opens with skepticism: 'That is not how harmless projects begin.' Frames Patch's overnight build as a suspicious pattern — the exact stance the memory encodes.

behavioral_manifestations.speaker: Patch
behavioral_manifestations.manifestation: 'It is harmless. Probably.' — the tell of unsettled details.

behavioral_manifestations.speaker: Rivet
behavioral_manifestations.manifestation: '"Interesting" is doing a great deal of work in that sentence. What message has it left?' — presses for observable/testable behavior instead of accepting Patch's framing.

behavioral_manifestations.speaker: Rivet
behavioral_manifestations.manifestation: 'those messages do not tell us whether it noticed anything useful.' — again pushes for testable behavior.

behavioral_manifestations.speaker: Rivet
behavioral_manifestations.manifestation: 'Change one thing: start a print. Then we see whether it reports an event, or merely develops a literary career.' — enforces the methodical experimental protocol the memory says Rivet has learned Patch skips.

behavioral_manifestations.speaker: Patch
behavioral_manifestations.manifestation: 'Look at that—its little light is blinking. Well… now I want to try it.' — the exact excitement→jump pattern the memory encodes.

behavioral_manifestations.speaker: Rivet
behavioral_manifestations.manifestation: 'Wait for the message.' — the memory-derived caution held in a single beat.

memory_influence_analysis.note: This is the character-DYNAMIC manifestation channel: Rivet embodies the wariness the memory names; Patch performs the very behavior Rivet has learned to anticipate. Neither character narrates that they are doing so. The memory shapes the WAY they interact rather than adding a new fact to the scene.

visual_beat_classification_for_this_scen.reasoning: Rivet's opening line describes the tableau verbally; the description sufficient for the beat to land. A cutaway would add texture, not information.

visual_beat_classification_for_this_scen.moment: line 3 — the three cited messages ('Printer thinking.' etc.)
visual_beat_classification_for_this_scen.reasoning: Payload lands as spoken content in Patch's voice; a text/quote overlay could add polish but the beat is intact without one.

Avatar's natural downward glance while saying 'its little light is blinking' supplies enough implied physicality that the absent insert is not strongly felt (per operator observation). A close-up on the blinking light would enhance.

visual_beat_classification_for_this_scen.moment: line 11 — final quoted message 'Patch is watching me watch it.'
visual_beat_classification_for_this_scen.reasoning: Landing lives in the character reaction. A text overlay of the message could reinforce, but the beat lands as spoken content.

visual_beat_classification_for_box_scene.moment: line 0-1 — Patch physically blocking Rivet's view of the box
visual_beat_classification_for_box_scene.reasoning: The physical block IS the beat. Dialogue references it but the beat cannot land without seeing it.

visual_beat_classification_for_box_scene.moment: throughout — the unopened box behind the 3D printer
visual_beat_classification_for_box_scene.reasoning: The box is the scene's visual center. Its physical presence and unopened state carry the tension. No shot = no visual center.

visual_beat_classification_for_box_scene.moment: line 16-18 — landing on 'You open it.' / 'I see. The experiment has already produced a result.'
visual_beat_classification_for_box_scene.reasoning: The ending's dramatic weight is on the visible artifact remaining unopened. Without the artifact on screen the landing is text alone.

refined_hypothesis.text: Dialogue scenes need visual beats when understanding or feeling the scene depends materially on something happening outside the talking heads.
refined_hypothesis.note: Box scene: visual object IS the scene → shot required. Helper scene: physical object exists but the dramatic payload is in the messages and the character dynamic → shot enhances. Both scenes contain physical props; the differentiator is where the meaning lives, not whether a prop exists.
refined_hypothesis.status: provisional — two-Episode support, not yet ratified as architecture

memory_promotion_candidate.text_chris_intends_to_consider: Patch built a workshop helper that watches for interesting events and leaves messages, but it has already started adding its own commentary to what it observes.
memory_promotion_candidate.distinction_from_box_scene: Box scene opened a hook without establishing durable state (unknown what the box is / what's inside / whether it's an experiment / whether it matters later). Helper scene establishes: (a) the artifact exists, (b) it has demonstrated behavior — messages including 'Printer thinking.', 'The room is suspiciously quiet.', 'Patch is watching me watch it.', (c) it has developed a commentary tendency Rivet has now named. All three are durable facts a future scene can reference.
